lede: “Perhaps you will grieve yourself to death because they do not believe.” To the man that was said to, the surah tells seven histories in a row, and closes each with the same two ayat: “In that is a sign, yet most of them were not believers. And your Lord — He is the Almighty, the Merciful.”

names.name: al-Shuʿarāʾ
names.note: After the poets of its closing ayat (26:224–227), set against the Prophet ﷺ whom Quraysh had called one of them. Ibn Kathīr notes that in the commentary transmitted from Mālik it is called Sūrat al-Jāmiʿah.

revelation.verdict: Makkan — its last four ayat are reported Madinan
revelation.detail: It is Makkan in the saying of the majority. Ibn ʿAbbās and Qatādah excepted four ayat, from “And the poets — the misguided follow them” to the end, which they said came down in Madinah; Ibn al-Jawzī and al-Qurṭubī both record this. Its command to “warn your nearest kin” is tied by the reports in the two Ṣaḥīḥs to the day the Prophet ﷺ climbed al-Ṣafā and called Quraysh clan by clan. With two hundred and twenty-seven ayat it has more than any surah but al-Baqarah, though its ayat are short. The traditional order places it forty-seventh.
revelation.when: The early and middle years in Makkah

evidence.quote: سُورَةُ الشُّعَراءِ وَهِيَ مَكِّيَّةٌ كُلُّها، إلّا أرْبَعَ آياتٍ مِنها نَزَلَتْ بِالمَدِينَةِ

attested.quote: سُورَةُ الشُّعَرَاءِ مَكِّيَّةٌ إِلَّا أَرْبَعَ آيَاتٍ
أخْرَجَ ابْنُ الضُّرَيْسِ، وابْنُ مَرْدُوَيْهِ، عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ قالَ: نَزَلَتْ سُورَةُ ”طسم الشُّعَراءِ“ بِمَكَّةَ
attested.says: Ibn ʿAbbās: it came down in Makkah. Recorded by Ibn al-Ḍurays and Ibn Mardawayh.

setting: The surah opens on the Prophet’s own state. He wanted his people to believe so much that it was consuming him, and he is told that if Allah willed He could send down a sign from the sky before which their necks would stay bowed. That is not how it is to be. They have already been given signs enough: “Have they not looked at the earth — how many of every noble kind We have caused to grow in it?”

What follows is seven stories, told fast. Mūsā before Pharaoh, at the greatest length; then Ibrāhīm and his people; then Nūḥ, Hūd, Ṣāliḥ, Lūṭ and Shuʿayb. The last five are cut to one pattern on purpose. Each messenger says the same words — “Will you not be mindful? I am to you a trustworthy messenger; so be mindful of Allah, and obey me. I ask of you no wage for it; my wage is only with the Lord of the worlds” — and then names the one wrong his own people were sunk in: Nūḥ’s people their contempt for the poor who followed him, ʿĀd their towers and their tyranny, Thamūd their luxury, the people of Lūṭ their indecency, the people of the Thicket their short measure. Each is refused. Each story ends with the refrain. By the eighth time, the listener knows it by heart.
The point for the Prophet ﷺ is in the refrain’s two names. Al-ʿAzīz: none of those peoples escaped. Al-Raḥīm: every one of them was sent a messenger first, and given time.

Then the surah turns to the Qurʾan and clears it of both things Quraysh called it. It is not the work of a soothsayer: “The devils have not brought it down; it is not for them, nor are they able.” And it is not poetry. The poets wander in every valley and say what they do not do — but this was brought down by the Trustworthy Spirit upon your heart, in a clear Arabic tongue.

And in the middle of that close stands the command that began the public call: “Warn your nearest kin.” Ibn ʿAbbās relates that when it came down, the Prophet ﷺ climbed al-Ṣafā and called out, “Banū Fihr! Banū ʿAdī!” — until the clans of Quraysh had gathered — and asked whether they would believe him if he told them of horsemen in the valley about to raid them. They said: we have never known you to say anything but the truth. He said: “Then I am a warner to you before a severe punishment.”

occasions.title: The call from al-Ṣafā
occasions.text: When “And warn your nearest kin” was revealed, the Prophet ﷺ went up al-Ṣafā and began to call: “Banū Fihr! Banū ʿAdī!” — the clans of Quraysh — until they had gathered; a man who could not come himself sent someone to see what it was. He said: “Tell me: if I informed you that horsemen in the valley were about to attack you, would you believe me?” They said: “Yes; we have never found you anything but truthful.” He said: “Then I am a warner to you before a severe punishment.” Abū Lahab said: “May you perish for the rest of the day! Is it for this you gathered us?”

aim: To confront those who persist in denying the Messenger ﷺ and attacking his message, and to show how little their standing is.
themes: The Qurʾan brought down by the Trustworthy Spirit

outline.title: Do not grieve yourself to death
outline.summary: Ṭā Sīn Mīm. These are the ayat of the clear Book. Perhaps you will destroy yourself with grief because they do not believe. If We willed, We could send down on them a sign from the sky, and their necks would remain bowed to it. Have they not looked at the earth — how many of every noble kind We have caused to grow in it? In that is a sign, yet most of them were not believers. And your Lord — He is the Almighty, the Merciful.

outline.title: Mūsā and Pharaoh
outline.summary: Your Lord called Mūsā: “Go to the wrongdoing people.” — “My Lord, I fear they will deny me; my chest tightens and my tongue does not run free.” Pharaoh said: “Did we not bring you up among us as a child?… And what is the Lord of the worlds?” The staff, and the hand. The sorcerers gathered, and fell prostrate: “We believe in the Lord of the worlds.” Then, at the sea, the companions of Mūsā said: “We are overtaken.” He said: “No. My Lord is with me; He will guide me” (26:62). And the sea parted, each part like a great mountain.

outline.title: Ibrāhīm, and his prayer
outline.summary: Recite to them the story of Ibrāhīm. “Do they hear you when you call? Do they benefit you, or harm?” — “We found our fathers doing so.” — “They are enemies to me, all but the Lord of the worlds: who created me, and He guides me; who feeds me and gives me drink; and when I am ill, He heals me; who will cause me to die and then give me life.” “My Lord, grant me judgement, and join me with the righteous… and do not disgrace me on the Day they are raised — the Day when neither wealth nor sons will avail, but only he who comes to Allah with a sound heart.”

outline.title: Nūḥ, and Hūd
outline.summary: The people of Nūḥ denied the messengers. “Shall we believe you, when the lowest follow you?” — “I am not one to drive away the believers.” We saved him and those with him in the laden ship. ʿĀd denied the messengers. “Do you build on every height a monument, in vanity? And when you strike, you strike as tyrants.” They said: “It is the same to us whether you preach or do not.” So We destroyed them.

outline.title: Ṣāliḥ, Lūṭ and Shuʿayb
outline.summary: Thamūd denied the messengers. “Will you be left secure in what is here — gardens and springs, and houses carved skilfully from the mountains?” They hamstrung the she-camel. The people of Lūṭ denied the messengers: “Do you approach the males of the worlds?” The people of the Thicket denied the messengers: “Give full measure, and weigh with a true balance.” — “Then make fragments of the sky fall upon us, if you are truthful.” The punishment of the day of shadow seized them.

outline.title: The Trustworthy Spirit, and the poets
outline.summary: It is the sending down of the Lord of the worlds: the Trustworthy Spirit brought it down upon your heart, that you may be of the warners, in a clear Arabic tongue; and it is in the scriptures of the ancients. Warn your nearest kin, and lower your wing to the believers who follow you. Put your trust in the Almighty, the Merciful, who sees you when you stand, and your movement among those who prostrate. Shall I tell you upon whom the devils descend? Upon every sinful liar. And the poets — the misguided follow them; they wander in every valley, and say what they do not do — except those who believe and do right, and remember Allah much.

keyAyah.why: The close of Ibrāhīm’s prayer, and the measure of the Day: nothing is brought to it but the heart.

virtues.text: When “And warn your nearest kin” was sent down, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood and said: “People of Quraysh, ransom yourselves; I can avail you nothing against Allah. Banū ʿAbd Manāf, I can avail you nothing against Allah. ʿAbbās son of ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, I can avail you nothing against Allah. Ṣafiyyah, aunt of the Messenger of Allah, I can avail you nothing against Allah. Fāṭimah daughter of Muḥammad, ask me for what you will of my wealth; I can avail you nothing against Allah.”
virtues.arabic: يَا فَاطِمَةُ بِنْتَ مُحَمَّدٍ سَلِينِي مَا شِئْتِ مِنْ مَالِي لاَ أُغْنِي عَنْكِ مِنَ اللَّهِ شَيْئًا

before: Al-Furqān recorded what Quraysh said against the Messenger, and ended: “You have denied.” Al-Shuʿarāʾ shows him seven who were denied before him.
after: Al-Shuʿarāʾ opens Ṭā Sīn Mīm and begins with Mūsā. Al-Naml opens Ṭā Sīn and begins with Mūsā — and then turns to those who did believe: Sulaymān, and the Queen of Sabaʾ.
